angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 469,598 km at 169.29 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.9070 +/- 0.0180 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 169.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.675 +/- 0.033 solar radii from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-121 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract): 469,598 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.71 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-121 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4526 +/- 110 K from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-121 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-121 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract)
